svg.title: Korvid low and high: separate behavior files, one shared engine
svg.desc: Low and high define their own prompts, tool surfaces and budgets. Low allows one call per round, focused reads and opening logs or details. High additionally offers navigation, filtering, drill-down and configured observability reads. Both tiers can request writes when enabled, but only actual user approval and the shared audit gate can authorize execution. ModelRouter selects policy, not a different agent. All accepted calls execute sequentially.
svg.text: Separate behavior. Shared execution and safety.
Low/high choose operating constraints for the selected model; they are not two collaborating agents.
Tier precedence: explicit setting > provider recommendation > shipped catalog > low fallback
Small, explicit steps and compact answers
Broader investigation and richer cited answers
1 accepted call per round / shorter tool descriptions
1 accepted call unless provider confirms multi-call*
The same cluster reads and diagnostics
Writes may be offered. Low does NOT mean read-only.
Writes obey exactly the same approval gate as low.
Session + PromptHarness + NativeAgentEngine + ConversationState + RequestGateway + ToolHarness
Registry-derived tools / readonly and capability gates / masking / evidence / interrupt and recovery
Writes: fresh user approval + in-flight reservation + persisted intent audit + UID-bound mutation + outcome audit.
* Only high + provider-reported supports_parallel_tools=true admits multiple calls. Accepted calls still run sequentially.
Default selection and behavior are preserved; this refactor separates definitions, not security boundaries.
